data.name: Lumberjack VR
data.detailed_description:
Experience the thrilling life of a Lumberjack in virtual reality with Lumberjack VR, an arcade action game for the HTC Vive. Fight your way through waves of logs, lumber and bombs with nothing but an axe in your hand.

Play in 3 levels, each with its own unique mechanics. Score as high as possible to continue to the next wave and to reach the top of the leaderboard. Each level consists of 5-10 waves. You must reach the target score to continue to the next wave before the timer hits zero. If you fail, you will be sent back to wave 1. You score points by chopping wood as straight and even as possible. You can also score points by hitting the massive target boards with bombs, performing ticks and more. If you struggle to compete on the leaderboards, you can hone your skills in the training levels to become a master Lumberjack.

Features

  • Immersive wood chopping
  • 5 unlockable axes
  • 3 levels with up to 10 waves per level
  • Global Leaderboards
  • 6 achievements

Get Lumberjack VR today and become a master Lumberjack!

reviews.review:
Lumberjack VR takes one of virtual reality’s most natural physical actions, swinging a tool with your hands, and builds an entire arcade challenge around it. Instead of presenting a detailed forestry simulator, the game concentrates on chopping, accuracy, reaction speed, and score chasing. Developed by Erik Brunnström and published by Erik Brunström, it is a deliberately compact VR experience that is easy to understand within minutes but becomes increasingly demanding once higher scoring requirements enter the picture.

The basic objective is to chop incoming pieces of wood while accumulating enough points to complete each wave. What makes the system more interesting than simply swinging wildly is the emphasis on the quality of each cut. Straighter and more accurate strikes can produce better results, encouraging controlled movements rather than frantic attacks. This creates a satisfying relationship between the player's real-world movement and the score appearing in the game. Getting the timing and angle right can feel rewarding, particularly after becoming familiar with how the game interprets each swing.

Progression is structured around three primary levels, with each one divided into multiple waves. Different mechanics are introduced as the player advances, preventing the challenge from consisting exclusively of identical pieces of timber. Bombs, for example, can be struck toward larger targets to earn additional points, adding another layer of timing and positioning. There are also opportunities to perform tricks and pursue more efficient scoring strategies. The mechanics remain straightforward, but players interested in maximizing scores have more to consider than simply making contact with every object.

Difficulty largely comes from the score requirements and the consequences of failure. Players must reach the required number of points within the available time, and failing a wave can result in restarting from the beginning. This gives the experience an unmistakably old-school arcade character. Successful runs depend on maintaining good performance across several challenges rather than barely surviving one encounter at a time. The downside is that repeatedly replaying earlier waves can become frustrating, especially when a mistake happens near the end of an otherwise successful attempt.

Additional motivation comes through unlockable equipment and competitive features. Five extra axes can be earned, giving players some rewards beyond simply improving a number on a leaderboard. Training stages provide opportunities to become comfortable with the chopping mechanics, while global leaderboards encourage competitive players to refine their technique and chase stronger performances. Steam achievements add another small collection of objectives. These systems do not dramatically expand the core gameplay, but they provide useful incentives for players who enjoy repeating short challenges until they achieve cleaner results.

As a physical VR experience, the game benefits considerably from its simple concept. Actually making chopping motions with tracked controllers creates an immediacy that would be difficult to reproduce with a traditional controller. The physical nature of the gameplay can make a short session energetic and entertaining, although repeated swinging can also become tiring. Players need to remain aware of their surroundings because enthusiastic movements can become fairly wide. The room-scale focus therefore makes an appropriately clear play area particularly important.

Visually, the game keeps things functional rather than extravagant. Its presentation is designed to support the arcade action instead of creating a realistic wilderness simulation. That simplicity fits the game's modest scope, but anyone expecting detailed environments, extensive progression systems, exploration, resource gathering, or a lumber business simulation will find the package considerably more limited. There is no substantial narrative campaign behind the chopping. The central attraction is improving at the mechanics themselves.

The relatively small amount of content is its biggest weakness. Three main levels can provide enjoyable challenges, especially for players who become invested in leaderboard competition, but the fundamental loop does not evolve enough to appeal equally to everyone over extended sessions. Repetition is unavoidable, and enjoyment depends heavily on whether improving scores and mastering accurate swings remains satisfying. Players who prefer extensive VR adventures will likely consider this more of a short arcade diversion.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsupported for normal Steam Deck play because Lumberjack VR is a VR-only title built around tracked motion controls and a SteamVR setup. The Deck's integrated controls and screen cannot reproduce the intended room-scale interaction on their own. Even if unconventional external VR configurations are technically attempted, this should not be considered a practical handheld Steam Deck experience.

Taken for what it is, Lumberjack VR offers a straightforward and physically engaging interpretation of arcade lumberjacking. Accurate chopping, increasingly demanding waves, special targets, unlockable axes, achievements, training options, and leaderboard competition give its simple premise enough structure to be entertaining in shorter sessions. Its restricted amount of content and repetitive progression prevent it from becoming a substantial VR experience, but players interested in uncomplicated score chasing and energetic motion-control gameplay can still find something enjoyable here.

Rating: 7/10
